segments.text: So Sinead, welcome back. How are you doing?
I'm good. I am very good. I'm feeling good, mentally, physically. I'm in a very good place.
Yeah, ready to get going now. It's been a while.
How does it feel to be back on court? What did you miss most when you were out injured?
I just miss everything there is about playing the sport. I miss the long hours in the gym,
I was going to say the aches and the pains, but I didn't really miss waking up sore,
but I miss that feeling of knowing that you've worked hard and you've put in a good shift
that day.
It's the feeling of being on a tennis court, like doing what I do best, you know, getting
back to my job.
Can you tell us a bit about the injury and the recovery process to this point?
Yeah, I had a part of the stress fracture.
It would have been six months that I'd been out for.
typically they range from about six to nine months depending on severity and
recovery wise but yeah it's been a long long process you know I think first
three months were slow not many not many changes kind of was almost just
stumped a bit didn't feel like I was going in the right direction and then
all of a sudden just really started to rock it upwards and it's been smooth
sailing the past few months yeah everything is feeling good my back is
and great. Everything around the back is feeling stronger so I feel good, I feel good.
What is something about dealing with a long term injury that fans and people in general
might not realise?
I think there's loads of things, I think for me it was my first one so you know, missing
throughout the four slams this year was incredibly tough, missing a home slam, incredibly tough.
Being an individual sport right, if I'm not on a tennis court, I'm not working,
and not earning. So you've got those things and just tennis is what I've known, right?
The past 18 years I've done it every day and just not being able to do that and just feeling
so like, you know, I couldn't do the basic of things. I couldn't brush my teeth without
kind of almost standing back up and just being in agony. So it was definitely a tough
injury but yeah it's definitely made me a stronger person, a better person and
hopefully it'll make me a better tennis player.
And has it meant you've been able to enjoy some time at home? What have you been up to outside of recovery?
I'll be honest I kind of feel a bit robbed of it because you know first month or two
I was just in quite a lot of pain so I couldn't really get away because it was just not
enjoyable to be out and about doing things and then past four months has
been Monday to Friday nine to five in the physio room in the gym getting back
to what I can you know I couldn't to make sure I'm back for this time I
couldn't really miss at the time I couldn't miss one or two weeks because
it would set me back you know I need to I need to get myself back in the match
court so I would do whatever it took and so yeah I've I mean I feel refreshed
without going away. Yeah a lot of the girls have reached out to me and just
checking in with me you know every couple weeks making sure I'm making
sure I'm doing good make sure I'm going the right direction mentally making sure
that I'm happy and keeping sane and they're not banging my head against the
wall so yeah they definitely looked out for me and you know I've kind of been
up at the National Centre for all the rehabs so I've still been in
the environment of the players and you know been into contact kind of with
everyone. Probably the most time I've spent with all of them actually. So yeah
everyone has been super supportive, giving me a lot of good advice and yeah
just making sure I'm all good.
Your results at the start of the year were really impressive. Do you still take positives from those results or does it feel like a bit of a reset now?
Yeah I think at the time I was doing great. Like I was feeling really good. I was
getting good wins. I was playing some some great tennis and I think things were
developing from the practice court nicely into the match court so yeah it
was definitely not the best thing that could have happened but you know you've
got to find the positives and the negatives and you know I've took this
time to kind of work on on other things in my body that my body didn't have
enough time to do so I think I'm kind of put the start of the year just to one
side you know and I'm starting fresh from from now.
In the head of the summer, posters on Instagram say Carts 2.0 coming soon, what do you think
Carts 2.0 will look like when you get back out there competing?
If you want to have a few more tattoos maybe, that could be one thing. But no, I'm still
going to be the same person, just hopefully a better version, hopefully I'm a better tennis
player, I'm a stronger tennis player. Hopefully everything that I was in March has just gone
up a level and I think mentally I've gone up a level you know this rehab is
tough you know you go through a lot of emotions a lot of roller coasters a lot
of highs and lows yeah I'd like to think there's gonna be a better a better play
around the court. And now you're back competing what does the rest of the year look like for you?
Yeah I'll be doing the Asian swing I'll be out there for a fair few weeks to
see if I can play a few tournaments in kind of December you know I'm having a
season that's a little bit back to front you know when everyone's kind of
during their pre-season, November, December,
I would have already done mine now.
So yeah, I'm just gonna try and keep playing,
make up for a bit of lost time.
And yeah, I'm hoping that I can finish the year
Christmas time kind of feeling,
feeling like the player I was when I had to stop
so I can go into next year feeling good
and feel as almost as if this hasn't happened,
it hasn't affected my tennis.
How excited are you to be joining up
for the Billie Jean King Cup squad for your first tournament back?
You know, for me, there was no better way to do it.
I think in in every interview, I say it's, you know, my favourite weeks of the year.
I love the team, the team atmosphere, the team events.
You know, I love spending time with the girls, such a unique event.
And yeah, I think it's going to be a great week personally.
I'm going to get some great sparring.
And yeah, it's a nice way to just dabble back into the to the tennis life.
And yeah, hopefully we can put in a good shift.
And what made you decide that now is the right time and how did those conversations go with
Anne before confirming your spot on the team?
You know, I had some choices to make.
I've been kind of good to go really from kind of US Open time.
You know, decided not to play that to almost just put my body under a bit more stress to
try and recreate a bit more of a match environment, you know, play two, three hours a day so
I can, you know, kind of match that up to match intense to as best as I could.
You know, I had the decision to go and play an event, you know, in Portugal or B.J.K.
You know, she left it up to me and it was for me to decide and if I feel like I'm good
to go and fit and healthy, then she said to me, I want you in the team.
So yeah, it took some time, decided on my decision and yeah, for me, you know, it's
the way I wanted to go back into it.
want to have this week with the girls as my first week in tennis you know I've
been good sideline for six months I think it's it's gonna be a very fun
week for me to be in that environment and you were such a big part of the
semi-final last year playing and winning your first
villaging cup matches what did you enjoy the most from that experience last year I
think you know playing those ties I remember the first time I played in
Netherlands people were saying to me you know you'll never forget the
nerves of your first tie and just the feeling because those matches mean more
to you than than other matches right you want to you want to do well for your
country you want to do well for the girls so yeah I was I was a ball of nerves in
those matches I think one match my body actually just cramps just from the
stress so I had to navigate that which was bizarre for me anyway but um yeah
it's they're special weeks they are truly special weeks I think you know
For me, Shenzhen last year, I was much better nervous-wise.
I think, you know, you just got to get your first tie out of the way
and then it's smooth sailing from there.
But I loved every second of those matches and, you know, we were so close.
So, yeah, I'm hoping this year we can go one step further.
And the team have made the semi-finals in three of the last four years.
So what makes this team such a special and unique team
and what's the atmosphere like?
The atmosphere is very fun there's a lot of good banter flying around a lot of
people that they bring a lot of noise and yeah keep people on their toes. Us
girls we spend a lot of time with each other here we spend a lot of time
training so we know each other very well we kind of know we know what things to
say what not to say we know what to say in the right moments I think we gel
really well that's one thing so I think it's just a mix of things you know
So we have a lot of fun, we've got them really well and I think we, depending on who plays,
we know the support they need and what they would want to hear from us on the court.
I think we get a lot of things right within the team.
